correctness.rationale: With the negative-frequency Zak convention in the record, applying −∂_z to the simple-pole series gives the squared-pole multiplier and the stated F. At lattice (1,1) the shifted/modulated windows correspond to multiplication of the orthonormal character basis by Zg; essential bounds for |Zg|² are therefore precisely the squared frame bounds. Z₁ is bounded and bounded away from zero on the one-sided rectangle. The cotangent circle has center −i coth(2πa) and radius csch(2πa); on its cap Im(cot)≥−1 the real part parametrizes a single graph on [−M,M], M=2/√(exp(4πa)−1). The zero requires real part −1/(πλ), with 2ω−1 equal to the imaginary part. This gives one boundary zero at equality and one open-cell zero above; ∂x Re F and ∂ω Im F are nonzero on this arc when λ≠0, giving simplicity. No zero occurs for λ=0. A boundary zero also kills the essential lower bound by interior continuity into every small neighborhood. Boundedness and nonvanishing almost everywhere prove Bessel and completeness. For positive λ near λc, the nonsingular real derivative in (x,ω) at the isolated critical zero, the uniform lower bound on |Z₁|, and an O(δ) trial residual force all weighted minimizers within O(δ) of the zero, δ=λc−λ. The constrained leading quadratic has its minimum at ω=0 and x−x*=M²δ/(M²+4), giving 4π²M²δ²/(M²+4). At contact Z₁(x*,0)=π(−M−2i), so the product is 4π⁴M²δ²=4π²(δ/λc)². Reflection x↦1−x handles negative λ, approaching each boundary only from the frame region. The finite supplied diagnostics were inspected, not executed; analysis, not the boundary-only numerical minimizer, proves the global asymptotic.

value.rationale: A derivative perturbation of a canonical rational Gabor window poses a natural stability problem at critical density. The exact interval and the distinct boundary/interior zero cases distinguish loss of stable reconstruction from loss of completeness. The sharp coefficient quantifies how rapidly the lower bound becomes unusable while still inside the frame region, with no pole-height dependence under the stated normalization. This is useful even without a full noncritical frame-set classification.
